title: Conflicts, client ID and screening
summary: The agent searches every party, alias and related entity against the firm's history, ranks the hits with a reason for each and drafts a clearance memo. It also collects and checks client ID under By-Law 7.1 and proposes ethical walls. A lawyer signs off on each conflict result, each consent or waiver, each ID verification and each wall. No matter opens and no money moves until those gates clear, and every search and decision lands in an append-only audit log.

screens.name: New conflict check
screens.purpose: Collect every party to search and start a check, usually pre-filled by the agent from an intake.
screens.layout: Left: the source (lead, intake or matter) and a short matter description. Centre: an editable party list with a role, aliases and related entities on each row. Right: the search scope and a preview of the parties the agent suggests adding.

actions.note: Pulls parties out of the intake narrative, documents and corporate registry lookups

actions.name: Add or remove a party
actions.note: Every change is logged

actions.name: Run check
actions.note: Starts the search. A clerk may run it, but only a lawyer clears it.

actions.name: Start from a matter being created
actions.note: 'Save and run check' path; matter stays draft until G2

screens.agent: Reads the intake, extracts every named person and organization with a proposed role, expands aliases (name variants, transliterations, initials, legal suffixes such as Inc/Ltd/Corp) and proposes related entities from public registry data. Each suggestion is labelled as proposed until a human keeps it.
screens.gate: none (the run itself is not gated; clearance is gated on conflict-clearance)
edge: Prospect gives only a first name or a nickname for the adverse party: the agent marks the party 'insufficient identifiers' and the check cannot be cleared until it is completed or a lawyer accepts the gap
The adverse party is unknown at intake (for example, an unnamed defendant): the check is saved with a placeholder and re-runs automatically once the party is named
Duplicate parties entered under two roles: merge them, keeping both roles
Non-Latin names: store the original script and the transliteration, and search both
screens.reg: RPC 3.4 conflicts and RPC 3.3 confidentiality (verify rule numbers). Information from a prospective client can itself create a conflict, so the matter description is minimal and access to it is restricted.

screens.name: Conflict results review
screens.purpose: Review the ranked hits for one check and mark each one relevant or not relevant, with a reason.
screens.layout: Top: the check header (parties, scope, run time, index version). Main: hits grouped by searched party, with the match score, match type, the firm record that matched and the agent's reason. Side panel: the matched record's details, limited to what the reviewer is allowed to see.

fields.name: hit.matched_record
fields.note: A contact, matter party, declined prospect or lateral-hire disclosure

fields.name: hit.match_type
fields.note: exact | alias | fuzzy | phonetic | related entity | shared identifier (address, phone, corp number)

fields.name: hit.matched_role
fields.note: The matched party's role on the other matter (client, adverse and so on)

fields.name: hit.other_matter_status
fields.note: open | closed | declined prospect

fields.name: hit.conflict_kind
fields.note: Agent proposal: direct adversity (current client) | former client, same or related matter | former client, confidential info | joint retainer | own-interest | prospective client info | none

fields.name: hit.reason
fields.note: The agent's one-line explanation of why this record matched and why it matters

fields.name: hit.disposition
fields.note: unreviewed | not relevant (false match) | relevant | needs lawyer

fields.name: hit.disposition_note
fields.note: Required when a hit scoring 80 or more is marked not relevant

fields.name: hit.found_in
fields.note: contact, party, lead, note, calendar, document, email, prospect

fields.name: hit.source_highlight
fields.note: Opens the matched record or document span side by side with the searched party

actions.name: Mark a hit not relevant
actions.note: Clerks may dismiss low-score false matches. Dismissing a high-score hit needs a note, and the lawyer sees it at sign-off.

actions.name: Propose dispositions
actions.note: Proposals only. The agent never sets a final disposition.

actions.name: Ask the responsible lawyer on the other matter
actions.note: Sends an internal query that reveals the party name only, never the new matter's facts

actions.name: Re-run with more parties
actions.note: Creates a new run version. The old results are kept.

actions.name: Send to lawyer for clearance
actions.note: Allowed once every hit has a disposition

actions.name: Duplicate and re-run
actions.note: New run on a lapsed or closed check, linked to the old one

screens.agent: Runs exact, alias, fuzzy (edit distance and token reordering), phonetic and shared-identifier matching across contacts, matter parties, closed matters, declined prospects and lateral-hire disclosures. Follows related-entity links one or two hops out. Ranks hits and writes a reason for each, proposes a conflict kind and disposition, and flags hits on walled matters without revealing walled content.
screens.gate: none (dispositions are reviewed again at clearance)
edge: A hit is on a matter behind an ethical wall the reviewer is screened from: show 'match on a restricted matter, refer to <lawyer>' with no details
Very common names (for example 'Mohamed Ali', 'John Smith') produce many hits: group them, and use DOB or address to rule them out
Corporate name reuse after amalgamation: link the predecessor and successor through the corp number
The index is still rebuilding after a bulk import: the run is flagged as incomplete and cannot go to clearance
A new contact is added to the firm while the check is open: the check is marked stale and the agent re-runs it
Hit is inside a document's text the reviewer cannot open (walled): shows 'restricted' and routes to compliance
screens.reg: RPC 3.4 covers current, former and joint clients and the duty to former clients (verify). Results are confidential: access is role-restricted and every view is logged.

rows: Former client on a lease matter; possible same-or-related
Parent company consulted the firm; check what was disclosed

screens.name: Clearance memo and sign-off
screens.purpose: The lawyer reads the agent's memo and records the decision: cleared, cleared with consent, decline, or cleared with a wall.
screens.layout: Left: the memo draft (facts, each relevant hit, analysis, recommendation). Right: the decision panel (outcome, conditions, signature) with a list of what is still outstanding.

fields.name: memo
fields.note: Agent draft. Every claim links back to a hit.

fields.name: outcome
fields.note: cleared | cleared subject to consent | cleared subject to screen | decline

fields.name: conditions
fields.note: For example: written consent from X; wall excluding Y

fields.name: rationale
fields.note: The lawyer's own words. It may adopt the memo, but adopting it is an explicit act.

fields.name: signed_by
fields.note: Must be a lawyer licensee who is not screened from any hit matter

fields.name: results_version
fields.note: Pins the exact run version that was reviewed

actions.name: Sign off
actions.note: Gate G2

actions.name: Decline and draft a non-engagement letter
actions.note: The agent drafts the letter. The lawyer approves the text, which must not disclose the conflicting client.

actions.name: Generate check report (PDF)
actions.note: Frozen snapshot of searches, hits, dispositions and sign-off; filed to the matter

screens.agent: Drafts the memo: parties searched, scope, each relevant hit with the applicable conflict category, and whether consent, a screen or a decline is indicated, citing the rule (verify). Lists open items such as an unreviewed hit or a missing identifier. On 'subject to consent' it creates the consent requests; on 'subject to screen' it drafts the wall.
screens.gate: G2: a lawyer signs the conflict outcome. Until then the matter cannot open, the engagement letter cannot be sent and no trust request can be issued.
edge: The signer is the lawyer on the conflicting matter: allowed, but the memo flags it (firm policy may require a second lawyer)
Data changes after sign-off (a new party, a new contact): clearance is marked stale and the agent requests a re-check
Sole practitioner: self sign-off allowed, logged like any other
Decline outcome: the prospect's information is kept for future checks but sealed (see the conflicts register)
Check lapses (auto-close) before sign-off: cannot be signed; must duplicate and re-run
screens.reg: RPC 3.4: some conflicts cannot be cured by consent, for example acting against a current client in the same matter (verify). The record of who cleared what, and when, is the firm's evidence for the LSO and LawPRO.

rows: Cleared subject to consent of Riverside Commercial Leasing Corp. (former client)
Former client 2023-0141; lease renewal on the same premises, so 'related matter' is likely
Declined prospect Hawthorne Holdings; intake note shows no confidential facts kept

screens.name: Consents and waivers
screens.purpose: Track every consent or waiver a clearance depends on, from draft through signed receipt.
screens.layout: List of consent requests, each showing who consents, its type, status and a link to the document. Detail drawer: the letter text, ILA (independent legal advice) recommendation, signature trail.

fields.name: consenting_party
fields.note: A current or former client, or a joint client

fields.name: consent_type
fields.note: acting against former client | joint retainer | advance waiver | consent to screen | other

fields.name: disclosure_summary
fields.note: What the party is told. It must not breach any other client's confidence.

fields.name: ila_recommended
fields.note: Whether the letter recommends independent legal advice

fields.name: document
fields.note: Signed letter

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft | approved | sent | signed | refused | withdrawn | expired

fields.name: scope_limits
fields.note: What the consent does not cover

actions.name: Approve letter text
actions.note: Gate G2a. A lawyer approves before it is sent.

actions.name: Send for e-signature
actions.note: Only after approval

actions.name: Chase
actions.note: Reminders on a schedule the lawyer sets

actions.name: Record oral consent
actions.note: Allowed only with a written confirmation sent afterwards (verify)

actions.name: Mark refused
actions.note: Sets the clearance to blocked

screens.agent: Drafts each letter from the memo with a factual disclosure, the risks, the right to refuse and an ILA recommendation. Checks the disclosure text against walled and other-client data and blocks it if the text would leak them. Sends it after approval, chases it and attaches the signed copy to the clearance.
screens.gate: G2a: a lawyer approves each consent letter's text before it goes out. The clearance becomes effective only when every required consent is signed.
edge: A consent is withdrawn mid-matter: the matter is flagged, the responsible lawyer is notified and the agent drafts withdrawal-options notes (RPC 3.7, verify)
An advance waiver given years ago is too vague for the current matter: the agent flags it rather than relying on it
Consenting party is an organization: record the signer's authority
screens.reg: RPC 3.4: consent must be informed, and joint-retainer consent has specific disclosure content (verify). Keep the signed consent on file.

screens.name: Conflict checks register
screens.purpose: Firm-wide list of every check, its outcome and its age, plus the sealed prospect records used in future searches.
screens.layout: Filter bar (status, lawyer, date, outcome). Table of checks. A side tab for 'Sealed prospects' (declined or unretained prospects kept for searching only).

fields.name: source
fields.note: Lead or matter

actions.name: Re-run stale checks
actions.note: Results go back through G2

actions.name: Export register
actions.note: Lawyer-only. The export is logged.

actions.name: Unseal a prospect record
actions.note: A lawyer gives a reason, for example a LawPRO claim

actions.name: Export CSV
actions.note: Same rule as export register

screens.agent: Nightly, re-runs open matters' party lists against parties added that day (the reverse check) and raises an alert when a new client conflicts with an existing matter. Lists checks waiting more than 2 business days for sign-off.
screens.gate: none (views only; exports and unsealing need a lawyer)
edge: Data imported from a previous system has no check record: shown as 'legacy, no check on file', with a one-click backfill check
A clerk searches the register for a name with no business reason: allowed by role, but every search is logged and visible to the admin
screens.reg: Keeping prospect data for conflict searching is a confidentiality and PIPEDA question: say so in the privacy notice (verify).

screens.name: Client identification (individual)
screens.purpose: Record who the client is (identification), and when funds will move, verify it, together with any third party the client acts for.
screens.layout: Top: obligation banner (identify only, or identify and verify, or exempt, with the reason). Left: identity fields. Right: the verification method panel with evidence. Bottom: third parties and history.

fields.name: business_address_phone
fields.note: If any

fields.name: occupation
fields.note: One or more

fields.name: dob
fields.note: Needed for the credit file method

fields.name: obligation
fields.note: identify only | identify + verify (funds) | exempt. Computed by the agent and confirmed by a human.

fields.name: exemption_reason
fields.note: client is the licensee's employer | agent for another licensee who identified the client | referred by a licensee who identified the client | funds-related exemption (see note) (verify list)

fields.name: funds_trigger
fields.note: The trust request or transaction that triggered verification

fields.name: verification_method
fields.note: government photo ID (in person, or virtual with authentication) | credit file (Canada, at least 3 years) | dual process (two independent reliable sources) | agent (verify)

fields.name: id_doc.number
fields.note: Stored encrypted and masked in the UI

fields.name: id_doc.issuer_place
fields.note: Jurisdiction and place of issue

fields.name: id_doc.expiry
fields.note: Must be valid on the verification date

fields.name: id_doc.copy
fields.note: Copy kept on file. Restricted access.

fields.name: authentication_result
fields.note: For virtual photo ID: passed | failed | manual review. Includes the vendor reference.

fields.name: verified_by
fields.note: Licensee, or a named agent with an agreement on file

fields.name: third_party
fields.note: Anyone the client acts for or represents, identified on the same basis

fields.name: source_of_funds
fields.note: Where the money comes from, recorded when verifying (verify)

fields.name: retention_until
fields.note: Computed: at least 6 years after the later of the end of the retainer and the last transaction (verify)

fields.name: risk_rating
fields.note: low | medium | high, with risk_reason; recorded at matter opening and again at closing

actions.name: Request ID from client
actions.note: Sends a portal link (see identity-portal)

actions.name: Determine obligation
actions.note: A proposal with a reason

actions.name: Confirm exemption
actions.note: A lawyer confirms why verification is not needed

actions.name: Record in-person check
actions.note: The licensee saw the original document and the person

actions.name: Confirm verified
actions.note: Gate G4

actions.name: Flag suspicion
actions.note: Opens a restricted note for the lawyer. The client is never told.

actions.name: Show KYC summary on matter
actions.note: Card on the matter with status, check dates and risk rating

screens.agent: Fills the identity fields from intake and the ID upload. Works out the obligation from the matter type and expected money flows, and when a trust request is drafted, flips the obligation to 'verify' automatically. Checks the document's validity dates, name and DOB consistency across sources, and the vendor authentication result. Screens names against Canadian sanctions lists. Lists gaps and computes the retention date.
screens.gate: G4: a lawyer confirms identification is complete and, where required, verification is done by an allowed method. Until then no trust receipt, payment or transfer can be posted on any of the client's matters.
edge: Funds arrive before verification: the receipt is held in a 'pending ID' state with an alert. The by-law allows verification within a period after the funds start moving (verify timing).
Virtual photo ID was only seen on a video call: rejected as insufficient since Jan 1 2024 unless it is authenticated
Credit file younger than 3 years, or its name or address does not match: the method fails, so try dual process
The client cannot produce ID (refugee, elder, minor): the lawyer records the alternative and the reason (verify what is allowed)
A returning client was verified years ago: reuse the verification if nothing has changed and it was already done (verify the reuse rule)
Name changed (marriage): link the former name for conflict searching
Risk rating at close differs from opening: the change and its reason are logged and shown on the card
screens.reg: LSO By-Law 7.1 Part III: identify every client when retained, and verify identity when receiving, paying or transferring funds, unless exempt (verify section numbers and the exemption list). Since Jan 1 2024, virtual photo-ID checks need authentication; credit file and dual process remain available (OBA summary; verify against LSO text). Records are kept for the period set by the by-law (verify the 6-year figure). Cash limits fall under By-Law 9.

screens.layout: Top: organization facts and the verification document. Middle: the people (authorized signers, directors, owners or controllers) in a table with the individual identity status of each. Bottom: the ownership chart and the agent's notes.

fields.note: Feeds conflict aliases

fields.name: org_type

fields.name: jurisdiction_and_number

fields.name: business_nature
fields.note: General nature of the business or activity

fields.name: instructing_individual
fields.note: Name, position and contact details of the person who gives instructions

fields.name: existence_evidence
fields.note: Certificate of status, articles, partnership or trust agreement (required when verifying)

fields.name: authorized_signers
fields.note: Individuals with authority to bind the organization on the matter (verify)

fields.name: directors
fields.note: Required when verifying (verify)

fields.name: owners_25pct
fields.note: Anyone owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, 25% or more (verify the threshold for By-Law 7.1)

fields.name: trust_parties
fields.note: For a trust: trustees, known beneficiaries and settlors (verify)

fields.name: ownership_structure
fields.note: How control is held

fields.name: bo_confirmation_steps
fields.note: Reasonable steps taken to confirm the beneficial ownership information (verify)

fields.name: exemption
fields.note: public body | reporting issuer | financial institution (verify)

actions.name: Pull registry profile
actions.note: Public corporate registry lookup

actions.name: Request beneficial ownership details
actions.note: Portal form for the instructing individual. Can ask for the corporation's register of individuals with significant control (Ontario private corporations keep one).

actions.name: Map ownership
actions.note: Builds the chart. Each layer is checked against registry data where it is public.

actions.name: Confirm organization verified
actions.note: Gate G4 (organization)

screens.agent: Pulls the registry profile, compares it with what the client gave, and lists directors and officers. Builds the ownership chart and flags opaque layers (a foreign holding company, nominee shareholders, bearer-style arrangements). Adds every director, owner and related company to the conflict party list and re-runs the check if new names appear. Runs sanctions screening on the organization and each owner.
screens.gate: G4 (organization): a lawyer confirms the organization's existence is verified and that the beneficial ownership record is complete or the gaps are explained. It blocks the same fund movements as the individual G4.
edge: Owners cannot be determined (a widely held private company or a chain of holding companies): record the steps taken and name the most senior managing officer instead (verify the fallback)
Registry data and client statements conflict: block and escalate
A numbered company with no operating name: generate searchable aliases
The organization changes control mid-matter: the agent watches registry changes on open matters
screens.reg: By-Law 7.1: organization identification, existence verification from an independent document, and beneficial ownership information when verifying (verify which provisions Ontario adopted from the Federation Model Rule and in what form). Ontario's 25% significant control register under the OBCA is a separate obligation on the corporation, but a useful source.

screens.name: Client ID upload (portal)
screens.purpose: A guided, mobile-first flow where the client provides identity details and documents for the firm.
screens.layout: Step-by-step on one column: 1 details, 2 document capture (front, back, selfie with liveness) or another method, 3 organization details if relevant, 4 review and submit. A firm-branded header names the lawyer who asked.

fields.name: personal_details
fields.note: Pre-filled from intake. The client confirms.

fields.name: method_choice
fields.note: photo ID with authentication | in-person appointment | dual process documents

fields.name: document_images
fields.note: Sent straight to the authentication vendor in Canada (verify vendor residency)

fields.name: dual_process_docs
fields.note: For example a utility bill plus a bank or CRA statement from two different sources

fields.name: consent
fields.note: Consent to collect and use the ID (privacy notice)

actions.name: Submit
actions.note: By the client

actions.name: Book in-person check
actions.note: Picks a slot on the firm calendar

actions.name: Validate and authenticate
actions.note: Calls the vendor and records the result

screens.agent: Validates image quality in real time, runs authentication through the vendor, extracts the fields, compares them with intake, and gives the client a plain-language reason when a step fails. It never states a legal conclusion to the client.
edge: Link forwarded to someone else: links are single-use, bound to an email or phone one-time passcode, and expire in 7 days
The vendor is down: offer dual process or an appointment
The client uploads an expired document: rejected with the reason
Accessibility: the flow must work with a screen reader and offer an in-person alternative
screens.reg: PIPEDA consent and purpose limitation for ID data (verify). ID images are kept only as long as By-Law 7.1 record keeping needs.

screens.name: Ethical walls
screens.purpose: Create, review and monitor screens that keep named people away from named matters, and enforce them across every module and the agent itself.
screens.layout: List of walls (matter, screened people, reason, status, breaches). Detail: the screened people, the protected matters, the undertakings, the access-attempt log and the notice to the affected client.

fields.name: screened_users
fields.note: Users who must not see the matters or work on them

fields.name: reason
fields.note: lateral hire (conflict from a former firm) | former client info | personal interest | consent condition | other

fields.name: origin_check
fields.note: The clearance that required the wall

fields.name: undertakings
fields.note: Signed by each screened user and each team member (verify that the rule requires this)

fields.name: client_notice
fields.note: Notice to the former client, where required (verify)

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft | pending approval | active | lifted

actions.name: Propose wall
actions.note: From a clearance outcome or a lateral-hire disclosure

actions.name: Approve and activate
actions.note: Gate G2b. A lawyer who is not screened approves.

actions.name: Collect undertakings
actions.note: E-sign

actions.name: Lift wall
actions.note: A reason is required

screens.agent: Drafts the wall from the conflict memo. Once it is active, enforces it everywhere: search, documents, email filing, time entry, calendar, reports and its own context. The agent never loads walled matter content into a session for a screened user, or answers that user's questions about it. Logs and alerts on blocked access attempts, and reminds the lawyer at each review date.
screens.gate: G2b: a lawyer approves each wall before it is active and each lift. Where the clearance depends on a wall, the matter cannot open until the wall is active and all undertakings are signed.
edge: The screened user is the only person with a needed skill: the wall stands, and the work goes elsewhere
Small firm (2-3 lawyers): the agent warns that a screen may not be adequate in a small firm and recommends considering a decline (verify against LSO commentary)
Shared mailbox or drive: walled content in shared spaces is flagged for clean-up
An admin with global access is screened: the wall overrides their role, and break-glass access needs a second lawyer and is logged
screens.reg: RPC 3.4 transfers between firms and the screening commentary; the CBA screening guidelines are commonly cited (verify Ontario rule numbers). The firm must be able to prove the screen was in place before the conflicted person arrived or the matter began.

screens.name: Lateral hire conflict disclosure
screens.purpose: Before a new lawyer, paralegal or staff member starts, record the matters they worked on at their former firm (at a high level) and check them against the firm's data.
screens.layout: A disclosure form (client names, adverse parties and general nature only) next to the agent's hit list and proposed walls.

fields.name: disclosed_matters
fields.note: Client, adverse parties, general nature, dates. No privileged detail (verify the limits on disclosure).

actions.name: Approve start conditions
actions.note: Gate G2c: walls active before the start date

screens.agent: Runs every disclosed party against the firm's current and former matters, proposes walls, and stores the disclosures, sealed, as a search source for future conflict checks.
screens.gate: G2c: a lawyer signs off on the lateral result. The joiner's account stays inactive until every required wall is active.
edge: The joiner refuses to disclose: escalate to the lawyer
Disclosure itself would breach a former client's confidence: allow a generic description
screens.reg: RPC 3.4 transfers between firms, and the duty not to disclose former-firm confidences (verify).

screens.name: Conflicts and ID audit log
screens.purpose: An append-only record of every search, view, disposition, sign-off, consent, ID access, wall change and blocked access in this area.
screens.layout: A filter bar (actor, human or agent, object, action, date) above a timeline table. Each row expands to show before and after values (sensitive values masked). Export button.

fields.name: at
fields.note: Server time, UTC, shown in local time

fields.name: actor
fields.note: A user, or the agent with the user it acted for

fields.name: action
fields.note: search | view result | disposition | memo edit | sign-off | consent event | id view | id download | verification | wall change | access blocked | export

fields.name: detail
fields.note: Masked. Never holds ID numbers or images, and never holds memo text, only a hash.

fields.name: hash_chain
fields.note: Tamper evidence

actions.name: Export for the LSO or LawPRO
actions.note: A lawyer approves. The export itself is logged.

actions.name: Weekly anomaly digest
actions.note: For example, unusual name searches or repeated blocked access

screens.agent: Writes every event, including its own actions, with the human on whose behalf it acted. Detects anomalies (searches unrelated to any intake, ID downloads in bulk, attempts on walled matters) and sends the digest to the admin and the responsible lawyer.
edge: Hash chain verification fails: alert the admin and lock exports
A retention expiry removes an ID record: the log keeps a 'destroyed per schedule' event, not the data
screens.reg: Proof of who cleared a conflict and when, and of By-Law 7.1 record keeping. The log is kept at least as long as the records it covers (verify).

screens.name: Client ID records and retention
screens.purpose: A firm-wide view of ID status for every active client and the retention or destruction schedule for ID records.
screens.layout: KPI strip (clients blocked on ID, verifications due, expiring documents, records due for destruction). Table of clients below, with tabs: Active, Blocked, Retention due.

fields.name: destruction_status
fields.note: not due | due | approved | destroyed

actions.name: Approve destruction batch
actions.note: Gate G14 (shared with closing)

screens.agent: Recomputes retention dates when matters close. Proposes destruction batches only for records past their date with no legal hold, and keeps a destruction certificate.
screens.gate: A lawyer approves each destruction batch.
edge: Legal hold or a LawPRO claim: destruction is suspended
The client has several matters: retention runs from the last one to end (verify)
screens.reg: By-Law 7.1 record retention (verify the period and its start event). PIPEDA requires that personal information is not kept longer than needed.

screens.name: Conflict search settings
screens.purpose: Decide what a conflict check searches, how loosely it matches, and how long checks and reports are kept.
screens.layout: Sections: Sources searched, Matching, Identifiers, Check lifecycle, Report. Each shows what it changes and a test search box.

fields.name: sources_searched
fields.note: contacts, parties on matters, leads, sealed prospects, notes, calendar entries, document names, document text, emails/communications, former-firm disclosures

fields.name: default_match
fields.note: similar (spelling, initials, transliteration) | exact; similar is default and cannot be off for names

fields.name: identifiers
fields.note: name, alias, email, phone, address, business number, DOB

fields.name: similarity_threshold

fields.note: An unresolved check lapses after N days (default 5); lapsed checks cannot clear a matter

fields.name: stale_after_days
fields.note: A cleared check older than N days must be re-run before opening the matter (default 30)

fields.name: max_parties_per_check
fields.note: No hard cap; warn above 25

actions.name: Change settings
actions.note: Lawyer-admin; every change is in the audit log with before/after

actions.name: Estimate impact
actions.note: Re-runs last month's checks with new settings, shows hits gained/lost

screens.agent: Runs the impact estimate; warns if a setting would hide hits that a lawyer previously marked relevant.
screens.gate: A lawyer approves any change that narrows the search.
edge: Someone turns off document-text search to speed things up: impact shows hits lost; requires approval
A new data source (email filing) is enabled: offer a one-time back-search of open matters
screens.reg: Rule 3.4 conflicts and LSO by-law record keeping: firm must have a reasonable system to check conflicts (verify).

rows: contacts, parties, leads, sealed prospects, notes, documents (text)

screens.name: Quick name search
screens.purpose: A fast pre-screen of one or two names while someone is on the phone, before any facts are taken.
screens.layout: Single search box with name and optional phone/email; result list grouped as client, adverse, prospect, other; button to turn into a full check.

fields.name: result_groups
fields.note: Only role and matter number shown, never facts

fields.name: reason
fields.note: Short reason; required for audit

actions.name: Start full check from this
actions.note: Carries names into conflict-check-new

actions.name: Stop the call script
actions.note: If an adverse hit, intake tells the caller the firm will call back

screens.agent: Runs on every incoming lead and phone note automatically and shows a traffic light on the lead.
screens.gate: none (it never clears anything; only G2 clears)
edge: Quick search shows no hits and staff treat it as cleared: screen states 'not a conflict clearance' and matter opening still requires G2
Screened user searches a walled matter's party: result says 'restricted, ask compliance' without details
screens.reg: Gather only enough to check conflicts before clearance (LSO Rules commentary to 3.4, verify).

screens.name: Party records cleanup
screens.purpose: Keep the conflict database accurate: merge duplicate people and companies, fill missing identifiers, and record relationships.
screens.layout: Tabs: Possible duplicates, Missing identifiers, Relationships. Each row shows two records side by side and the matters they touch.

fields.name: match_reason
fields.note: same email, same phone, similar name + address

fields.name: relationship
fields.note: spouse, parent/child, director, shareholder >25%, parent/subsidiary, employer, insurer, guarantor

fields.name: missing
fields.note: DOB, email, address, corporate number

actions.name: Merge records
actions.note: Lawyer approves; merge keeps both old names as aliases and all roles

screens.agent: Finds probable duplicates and relationships from registry pulls, documents and emails; never merges on its own.
screens.gate: Lawyer approves merges, because a merge can create or remove a conflict on an open matter.
edge: Merge would put adverse parties of two clients into one record: blocked and raised as a conflict
Two people truly share a name and DOB: 'not duplicate' is remembered
Undo a wrong merge: split restores both records and re-runs affected checks

entities.name: BeneficialOwner
relations: each person also gets an IdentityRecord when required

entities.note: stub added by spec lint: fields to be defined by the area owner

gates.name: Conflict clearance
gates.approver: lawyer (not screened from any hit matter)
gates.blocks: Opening the matter, sending the engagement letter, any trust request, any substantive advice

gates.name: Consent / waiver letter text
gates.blocks: Sending the consent. The clearance takes effect only when every consent is signed.

gates.name: Ethical wall activate / lift
gates.blocks: Opening a matter whose clearance depends on the wall; lifting any wall

gates.name: Lateral hire clearance
gates.blocks: Activating the joiner's account until required walls are active

gates.name: Client ID verified (individual or organization)
gates.blocks: Posting trust receipts, payments or transfers for the client; an exempt status also needs this approval

gates.name: ID record destruction
gates.blocks: Deleting ID documents and images past retention

agent_jobs.name: Party extraction
agent_jobs.trigger: event: intake submitted or document added to a matter
agent_jobs.does: Extracts named parties and roles, expands aliases and pulls related entities from the registry

agent_jobs.name: Conflict search and ranking
agent_jobs.does: Runs multi-method matching with related-party hops and ranks the hits with reasons
agent_jobs.output: Hit list with proposed dispositions for conflict-results

agent_jobs.name: Clearance memo
agent_jobs.does: Drafts the memo with categories, rule references (verify) and a recommendation

agent_jobs.name: Consent drafting and chasing
agent_jobs.does: Drafts the letters, then sends and chases them after approval

agent_jobs.name: Reverse conflict sweep
agent_jobs.does: Checks parties added today against all open matters and stale clearances
agent_jobs.output: Alerts and re-check requests (back through G2)

agent_jobs.name: ID obligation watcher
agent_jobs.trigger: event: trust request drafted or funds expected
agent_jobs.does: Raises the client's obligation to 'verify' and holds fund movement

agent_jobs.name: ID evidence check
agent_jobs.does: Authenticates the document, checks it for consistency, screens names against sanctions lists and lists gaps

agent_jobs.name: Beneficial ownership mapping
agent_jobs.does: Pulls registry data, builds the ownership chart and adds owners to the conflict parties
agent_jobs.output: Draft organization record for gate G4

agent_jobs.name: Wall enforcement and monitoring
agent_jobs.trigger: event: any access to a walled matter, plus schedule: review dates
agent_jobs.does: Blocks access, logs it and alerts; sends review reminders

agent_jobs.name: Expiry and retention
agent_jobs.does: Flags expiring ID documents on open matters and proposes destruction batches

agent_jobs.name: Audit anomaly digest
agent_jobs.does: Reviews the audit log for unusual searches, downloads and blocked-access patterns
agent_jobs.output: Digest for the admin and lawyer

agent_jobs.name: Duplicate and relationship finder
agent_jobs.does: Finds probable duplicate party records and missing relationships
agent_jobs.output: Suggestions on party-records-hygiene for lawyer merge approval

open_questions: Fuzzy-match threshold: below what score may a clerk dismiss a hit without lawyer review (proposed: 80)?
Should a sole practitioner's self sign-off need any extra step, or is the log enough?
Which ID authentication vendor, with Canadian data residency, and is its result accepted as 'authentication' under the 2024 LSO change?
Sanctions screening: which lists (Canadian consolidated autonomous sanctions list, SEMA, JVCFOA), and do we include politically exposed persons even though By-Law 7.1 may not require it?
Should declined prospects be kept indefinitely for conflict searches (sealed), or purged after N years?
Small firms: should the app refuse to activate a wall in firms below N lawyers, or only warn?
Are the agent's own reads of walled matters (on behalf of a screened user) blocked at the platform layer (per-session policy) or only in the app?
Need a lawyer review of the By-Law 7.1 exemption list, timing for verification after funds move, and the retention period before we hard-code them
Auto-close after 5 days and stale after 30: are these the right defaults for the firm?
Should email bodies be searched in conflict checks or only sender/recipient addresses?
'Share check' in-app link to any user allowed to see the check (walled users excluded), logged? (could)
Require an explicit acknowledgement when the clearance outcome differs from what hit dispositions imply? (could)
sources: https://lso.ca/about-lso/legislation-rules/by-laws/by-law-7-1 (primary; returned 403 to the fetcher, so it was not read)
